title: Raster tray icons for Flatpak apps that only exist in the Flatpak app bundle aren't displayed
line: Tray icons of Flatpak apps like Steam that ship their own icon files now show up instead of an empty space.
explanation: Flatpak apps such as Steam send an IconThemePath like ~/.local/share/Steam/public, which only exists inside their sandbox (on the host it lives under ~/.var/app/<id>/). The system tray handed that path to its icon loader as-is, so the icon was never found and the item stayed empty. When the sender is a Flatpak and the path does not exist on the host, the tray now looks it up through the app's own root, /proc/<pid>/root/<path>.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: find icon theme paths inside Flatpak sandboxes

Flatpak apps such as Steam send an IconThemePath that only exists inside
their sandbox, so their tray icon was empty. When such a path is missing
on the host, look it up through the app's root in /proc instead.

BUG: 442153

media.caption: Sandboxed tray app with its icon only inside the sandbox: nothing in the panel or the expanded tray
Same app with the fix: its red icon shows in the panel

review.text: Looking up the path through /proc/<pid>/root is the right idea, but the pid comes from servicePid(), which for Flatpak apps with a filtered session bus (the default, likely including Steam) is the xdg-dbus-proxy, whose own bwrap root has /.flatpak-info but not the app's files. The rig modelled the sandbox with a bare bwrap talking to the bus directly, so it never exercised the proxy case.
changes: Resolve the app's own pid from the Flatpak instance (e.g. $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/.flatpak/<instance-id>/bwrapinfo.json 'child-pid') and use that /proc/<pid>/root, or map $HOME paths to ~/.var/app/<app-id>/.
Test with a real Flatpak (or a bwrap app behind xdg-dbus-proxy).
